rows.why: S1 is spread over items 1 (header), 2 (row order) and 12 (BOM and CRLF). Item 12 is closest because it settles two of S1's four clauses: the BOM and CRLF after every row, including the last. Its ran output starts with the BOM and ends each line with \r\n. The header and the createdAt-then-id order shown in items 1 and 2 also match S1.

No item asks how status labels or dates are formatted for display. Item 9 is the only fit, and only for the missing-title clause, which it handles as S2 expects (empty field). But its ran output writes status as 'open' rather than 'Open' and createdAt as a full ISO timestamp rather than a YYYY-MM-DD date, both against S2.
Item 12 says what an empty list returns. Its ran output for [] is the BOM and the header row followed by \r\n, nothing else, which is what S3 expects.

Item 10 asks how fields with separators are quoted. Its ran output wraps the field and doubles inner quotes for a comma, quote and \n, as S4 says. But the pick, 'RFC 4180', doesn't cover S4's rule that a field starting or ending with a space must also be quoted, and RFC 4180 doesn't require that, so its behaviour there can't be told.
Item 11 asks whether formula-leading characters are neutralised. The pick does nothing: its ran output writes =SUM(A1) and +1 as they are, with no leading single quote as S5 requires.

S6 lists four refusal cases, each the subject of its own item: 3 (unknown status), 4 (bad counts), 5 (filled > openings) and 7 (invalid creation time). Item 3 is named, but every one of these items throws an Error naming the id, as their ran outputs show, which matches S6.
